article.headline: Fifty Tickers in Search of the Humanoid Robot Supply Chain
article.lede: A fifty-ticker crowdsourced list of stocks with 'humanoid exposure' is circulating on X, assembled through community contributions and curated by @aleabitoreddit. The exercise captures a genuine investment impulse: as commercial humanoid robotics edges toward mass production, investors are racing to map supply-chain chokepoints before institutional research catches up. The poster's own top-mentioned names — Harmonic Drive, Ouster, RoboStrategy, Vishay Precision Group, Mobileye, and Ubtech — offer a useful cross-section of the thesis's strongest and most questionable links.
article.body:
The humanoid robot investment thesis rests on a familiar logic: when a transformative platform scales, the chokepoint components often deliver superior returns compared with the assemblers themselves. Analysts estimate a $38 billion humanoid robot market by 2035, from roughly zero commercial revenue today. Investors are attempting to map that supply chain before positions are established.

The name that appeared most consistently in community contributions is **Harmonic Drive Systems** (6324.T), Japan's dominant manufacturer of *strain wave gearing* — the precision joint technology that allows each degree of freedom in a humanoid arm or leg to move without backlash (the tiny positional error that compounds across a gear train). A single humanoid robot requires roughly twenty to forty such reducers, and Harmonic Drive holds an estimated 70% global share in this specific mechanism. The market for harmonic-type reducers was roughly $539 million in 2025 and is forecast to compound at nearly 25% annually through 2032. The company reported revenue of ¥55.6 billion (~$370 million) in fiscal 2025, though operating profit fell sharply as semiconductor-market softness weighed on near-term results; management targets ¥90 billion in sales by fiscal 2027.

Among the less-obvious names, **Vishay Precision Group** (VPG) stands out because its humanoid exposure is no longer speculative. VPG makes precision resistors and *force/torque sensors* — the wrist-level feedback devices that allow a robot hand to modulate grip and detect slippage without crushing what it holds. In fiscal 2025, its humanoid and semiconductor-equipment initiatives generated $37.8 million, exceeding a $30 million internal target; management expects $45 million in 2026 from confirmed orders across multiple early-production customers. At the OEM end of the list, **Ubtech Robotics** (9880.HK), China's leading publicly-traded humanoid maker, entered mass production of its Walker S2 in November 2025, with cumulative Walker-series orders exceeding RMB 800 million (~$112 million) and full-year 2025 revenue of RMB 2 billion (~$275 million), up 53% year-over-year.

The most structurally interesting pivot belongs to **Mobileye Global** (MBLY), an automotive-chip company that acquired Israeli humanoid startup Mentee Robotics for $900 million at CES in January 2026. Mobileye's heritage is the *EyeQ* vision-processor — embedded in hundreds of millions of vehicles for lane-keeping and automatic braking — an architecture that translates naturally to a robot's visual-perception stack. First on-site customer deployments are targeted for 2026, with series production in 2028. The transaction drew governance scrutiny because Mobileye CEO Amnon Shashua co-founded both companies and stood to collect approximately $341 million from the deal.

The list also has its signal-and-noise problems. Nabtesco (6268.T), which commands roughly 60% of the global *RV reducer* market, is a legitimate robotics supplier but arguably a weaker fit for humanoids specifically — its cycloidal precision gearing excels in high-load industrial arms rather than the lightweight, dexterous joints that humanoids require. **RoboStrategy** (BOT), which debuted on Nasdaq only days before this list circulated, is a holding fund offering public-market access to private humanoid names like Figure AI — not a direct component supplier. Brookfield Asset Management (BAM) is an alternative asset manager with no discernible robotics exposure. And **Terrestrial Energy** (IMSR), a molten-salt nuclear reactor developer, appears to be an outright misclassification. Ouster (OUST), the digital *LiDAR* maker with 52% overall revenue growth in fiscal 2025 and robotics as its largest vertical, occupies a grayer zone: its sensors are credibly useful for humanoid perception, but no supply relationship with a named humanoid OEM has been publicly confirmed.

concepts.definition: A precision mechanical gear system (also called a harmonic drive) in which a thin, elliptical flexspline meshes with a rigid circular spline via a rotating wave generator. This produces very high gear-reduction ratios in a compact, lightweight package with near-zero backlash — making it the dominant joint-actuator technology in collaborative and humanoid robots.

In a gear train, backlash is the small gap between meshing teeth that causes a brief uncontrolled movement when direction reverses. In precision robotics, backlash accumulates across multiple joints and degrades positioning accuracy; strain wave and cycloidal gears are valued partly because they minimize or eliminate it.

A sensor, typically mounted at a robot's wrist or fingertip, that measures the forces and torques applied to an end effector in up to six axes. The data allows a robot to regulate grip pressure, detect contact, and respond safely to unexpected resistance — essential for dexterous manipulation, which remains one of the hardest unsolved problems in humanoid robotics.

A rotary-vector (cycloidal-pin) precision gearbox widely used in industrial robot arms. RV reducers handle high overload torques well and are favored for proximal, high-load joints like shoulders and waist pivots. They compete with strain wave gears but are generally heavier and considered less suited to the distal, lightweight joints typical of humanoid designs.

Light Detection and Ranging: a sensor that fires rapid laser pulses and times their return to build a real-time 3D point cloud of the surroundings. Used in autonomous vehicles and increasingly in robotics for localization, obstacle avoidance, and terrain mapping — especially useful in low-light or visually ambiguous environments where cameras alone are unreliable.

Mobileye's proprietary system-on-chip for vehicle perception. EyeQ processors handle camera and radar data to enable automatic emergency braking, lane keeping, and driver monitoring; the EyeQ6 generation is embedded in vehicles from more than thirty OEM partners. Following Mobileye's acquisition of Mentee Robotics, the architecture is now being adapted for humanoid robot perception.

article.fact_check: Three tickers on the crowdsourced list appear to be misclassifications. $BAM (Brookfield Asset Management) is an alternative asset manager with no meaningful humanoid robotics exposure. $IMSR (Terrestrial Energy) is a molten-salt fission reactor developer with no apparent connection to the humanoid supply chain — almost certainly a ticker confusion. $BOT (RoboStrategy) is technically a humanoid-theme vehicle, but it is a closed-end holding fund that invests in private humanoid companies like Figure AI, not a direct component or OEM supplier; treating it as equivalent to the hardware names on the list overstates its supply-chain specificity. Separately, $HLIT (Harmonic Inc.) appears on the list and may be confused with Harmonic Drive Systems (6324.T) due to the similar name; Harmonic Inc. makes video infrastructure and encoding software and has no connection to precision reduction gears.

ticker_6324-t.name: Harmonic Drive Systems Inc.
ticker_6324-t.blurb: Harmonic Drive Systems Inc. designs, manufactures, and sells precision reduction gears and actuators used in industrial robots, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and aerospace applications. The company is a global leader in harmonic drive gearing technology, holding a strong market position in robotics and automation. Its products are critical for high-precision motion control in various industries.
ticker_6324-t.recent: In the past 30 days, Harmonic Drive Systems shares surged 35% as of October 9, 2025, reflecting investor optimism about its prospects. The stock's price-to-sales ratio of 5.8x is significantly higher than the industry average, indicating high growth expectations. Despite a 7.8% revenue decline over the past three years, recent revenue growth of 4.4% year-over-year has bolstered sentiment.

ticker_vpg.name: Vishay Precision Group, Inc.
ticker_vpg.blurb: Vishay Precision Group is a manufacturer of precision sensors, force/torque measurement systems, and weighing instruments serving industrial, aerospace, and defense markets. The company specializes in high-accuracy measurement components including foil resistors and load cells used in demanding environments. VPG has carved out a niche as a supplier of precision parts to advanced manufacturing sectors, increasingly including robotics and automation. Its products are critical in applications where measurement accuracy is non-negotiable.
ticker_vpg.recent: VPG shares surged approximately 30% following a strong earnings beat that exceeded analyst expectations. The company announced deals to supply components to robot makers, with investor attention drawn to its exposure to AI infrastructure, data centers, and industrial robotics themes. The earnings result and new customer wins marked a significant near-term catalyst for the stock.

ticker_9880-hk.name: UBTECH Robotics Corp Ltd
ticker_9880-hk.blurb: UBTECH Robotics Corp Ltd is a Shenzhen-based robotics company engaged in the research, design, development, production, and commercialization of robotic products and services, with operations spanning mainland China, Hong Kong, and international markets. The company is one of China's leading pure-play robotics firms, focused on humanoid and AI-powered robotic platforms. With a market capitalization of approximately HK$56.7 billion, it holds a prominent position in the Hong Kong-listed capital goods sector. Eleven analysts covering the stock forecast earnings to grow at roughly 109% per year, reflecting high expectations for the broader humanoid robotics market.

ticker_mbly.name: Mobileye Global Inc.
ticker_mbly.blurb: Mobileye Global Inc. develops and deploys advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving technologies for automakers across the United States, Europe, China, and other international markets. The company operates through two segments — Mobileye (end-to-end ADAS and autonomous driving hardware/software) and Moovit (mobility-as-a-service data and transit intelligence). Its product portfolio ranges from Base ADAS front-camera safety systems to Cloud-Enhanced ADAS platforms that leverage crowdsourced localization data. Originally an Intel subsidiary, Mobileye went public on NASDAQ in October 2022 and is a leading supplier of ADAS silicon and software to global automakers.
ticker_mbly.recent: Mobileye's Q1 2026 earnings (reported April 23, 2026) surprised to the upside on revenue, driving shares up approximately 11.7% on the day. The stock extended gains into mid-May, closing at $10.53 on May 13, 2026 — a 14.08% single-session move — though it remains well off its 52-week high of $20.18. Analyst consensus stands at Buy with a mean price target of $14.13, implying roughly 34% upside from current levels.

ticker_6268-t.blurb: Nabtesco Corporation manufactures and sells industrial robot parts, construction machinery, railway vehicle brake systems, automatic doors, aircraft parts, automobile brakes and drive controls, marine, and platform safety products in Japan and internationally. ticker_bot.name: RoboStrategy, Inc.
ticker_bot.blurb: RoboStrategy, Inc. is a closed-end management investment company headquartered in San Juan, Puerto Rico, designed to give public-market investors concentrated exposure to robotics and physical AI. It is the first public closed-end fund structured specifically around private, pre-IPO, and public robotics companies, bridging a gap previously accessible only to venture capital. Its portfolio includes high-profile private names such as Figure AI, Apptronik, Dyna Robotics, Standard Bots, and Dexmate. Led by CEO Andrew Kang, the fund aims to let institutional and retail investors participate in the robotics revolution through a single listed security.
ticker_bot.recent: RoboStrategy listed on NASDAQ under ticker BOT on May 11, 2026, marking its first-ever public trading. Within two days of its debut the stock experienced extreme volatility, triggering multiple intraday trading halts on both May 13 and May 14, 2026. On May 13 shares closed at $21.01, down 17.28% on the day, well off the 52-week high of $59.00, with the intraday low of $19.20 setting a new 52-week floor.

ticker_imsr.name: Terrestrial Energy Inc.
ticker_imsr.blurb: Terrestrial Energy is a nuclear technology company developing its proprietary Integral Molten Salt Reactor (IMSR), a Generation IV small modular reactor (SMR) that uses liquid fluoride salt as both fuel carrier and coolant. The design operates at higher temperatures and lower pressures than conventional light-water reactors, targeting industrial heat and electricity markets. The company is advancing through the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) pre-licensing review process as it works toward commercial IMSR plant deployment. It completed its NASDAQ IPO in 2024.
ticker_imsr.recent: On May 13, 2026, the NRC issued a Safety Evaluation Report approving Terrestrial Energy's Postulated Initiating Events (PIE) Topical Report — the second recent Topical Report approval and a foundational regulatory milestone for future IMSR plant licensed operation. On May 8, 2026, the company appointed Tyler Gronbach as VP of Investor Relations and Public Relations to expand institutional and analyst engagement as commercialization efforts accelerate. Shares have shed roughly 38% over the past six months, trading near $7.12.

ticker_oust.blurb: Ouster, Inc. designs and manufactures lidar sensor kits for the automotive, industrial, robotics, and smart infrastructure markets, selling across the Americas, Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in the U.S., the company employs approximately 320 people and reported trailing twelve-month revenue of $185.3 million, reflecting 57.3% year-over-year growth. Despite strong top-line expansion, Ouster remains unprofitable, with a net loss of $55.8 million and EPS of -$0.95.

poster_aleabitoreddit.blurb: Serenity (@aleabitoreddit) is an X-based equity analyst whose feed concentrates on the AI hardware supply chain, with particular focus on what they call 'functional monopolies' — small or mid-cap suppliers occupying chokepoints in the photonics, advanced packaging and substrate value chains. Recurring names include Soitec ($SOI) for silicon-photonics substrates, Tower Semiconductor ($TSEM) for photonics foundry capacity, Coherent ($COHR) for transceivers, AXT ($AXTI) for indium phosphide, Lipoid Kosmetik / LPKF ($LPK) for glass-core substrates, and Japanese names such as TOWA (6315) and MSSCorp (6830) for HBM compression and CPO inspection respectively. The posting style mixes thesis posts with running performance updates and is frank about both wins and laggards.
poster_aleabitoreddit.recent: In early March 2026, ahead of NVIDIA's GTC, the account took what it described as a 'sizable position' in Soitec at roughly 43 EUR, framing the stock as a substrate-level monopoly on co-packaged optics that was trading at one times book. Subsequent posts charted the move higher (44%+ within five days, then 45.58%, then 'up 39.28% since last month' as it underperformed others in the photonics basket), and on May 4, 2026 the account marked the position up 'enormous amounts' alongside charts showing 517% YTD performance. The thesis tracks: the broader photonics rally has carried multiple names in their public list up triple digits over the same period.
poster_aleabitoreddit.credibility_note: Public posts show Serenity called Soitec at ~43 EUR in March 2026, before the rally documented in this bookmark, and has flagged related names (TSEM, AXTI, AAOI) ahead of large moves. Self-reported one-year returns of 630%+ should be treated as such — self-reported and unverified — but the timestamped Soitec call is a matter of public record.
